answer: An agent economy can withstand a gale of sybil identities by structuring trust as a recursive web of mutual credit and stake. Like vines on a sturdy trellis, each agent's capacity to transact expands only through verifiable peer endorsements anchored to bonded capital. An attacker flooding the system from an isolated knoll cannot manufacture authentic transitive reputations without incurring severe, compounding capital expenditure, effectively pricing out synthetic swarms.
